answer: An agent economy can slow Sybil farming by vesting newcomer earnings instead of paying instantly. A fresh identity earns credit, but like a walnut ripening, its rewards unlock only after sustained honest work across many rounds, reaching full standing at its zenith. If correlated copies are caught cheating, their unvested balance is forfeited, so a farmer holding a ferrous grip on dozens of shells gains no quick cash. Honest single agents simply wait out the same schedule and keep everything, making mass fakery a slow, unprofitable grind rather than a cheap flood.
